statement: The system shall support multiple user roles for the Publications Management System.
Regular researchers or staff shall be able to search publications.
Regular researchers or staff shall be able to upload new publication records or full texts for their own work.
Regular researchers or staff shall be able to download records or documents they have access to.
Editors or faculty admins shall be able to correct metadata.
Editors or faculty admins shall be able to merge duplicate publication records.
Editors or faculty admins shall be able to review uploads before they become visible more widely.
Moderators or librarians shall be able to approve publication information.
Moderators or librarians shall be able to reject publication information.
Moderators or librarians shall be able to adjust publication information.
Moderators or librarians shall be able to handle exceptions.
Moderators or librarians shall be able to manage author or institution name reconciliation.
Access to records shall be determined by both role and the scope of the record.
Authors or contributors shall be able to view all public records and edit only the items they own or submitted.
Faculty admins shall be able to edit records within their faculty.
Faculty admins shall be able to approve routine changes.
Moderators or librarians shall have the highest operational rights.
Moderators or librarians shall be able to approve records.
Moderators or librarians shall be able to correct metadata across faculties when needed.
Ownership shall apply to draft or newly uploaded records.
The submitter shall be able to revise draft or newly uploaded records until they are approved.
Once a record is published or approved, normal users shall not overwrite it directly.
When a published or approved record needs changes, normal users shall create either a correction request or a new version depending on the workflow.
Drafts shall be visible only to the owner and reviewers.
Approved records shall be broadly searchable.
Rejected records shall stay hidden except for audit purposes.
The system shall support a simple lifecycle with an initial draft or imported state in which a record is created but not yet validated.
The system shall move a record into review when a user submits it or when a bulk import is processed.
Approved records shall become published and searchable for everyone with access.
If later corrections are needed, the system shall support either an updated version replacing the old one or a correction status that preserves history.
If a publication is superseded by a newer version, the system shall mark the old publication as replaced rather than deleted to preserve traceability.
Before accepting an imported record, the system shall check that the core bibliographic fields are present and valid.
Before accepting an imported record, the system shall verify the presence and validity of title, authors, year, and at least one identifier if available.
Before accepting an imported record, the system shall perform format checks on dates, DOI or ISBN patterns, file types for uploads, and basic consistency between the extracted text and the metadata.
Before accepting an imported record, the system shall perform duplicate detection against existing records and alternative author or institution names.
The system shall apply a confidence threshold rule for extraction confidence.
High-confidence items may go straight into the review queue or be auto-accepted for very simple cases.
Low-confidence or incomplete records shall not be published automatically and shall be sent to a moderator or librarian for manual checking.
If the quality is too poor, the system shall reject the item or flag it as unusable rather than letting it clutter the database.

The system shall reduce inconsistencies.
